newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera postpones address on Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera postpones address on Colombia.

text.p: Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera postponed a planned address on relations with Colombia on Wednesday after a powerful earthquake hit the country, killing at least 20 people.
A presidential palace spokesman said the broadcast had been postponed and no new date had been set.
A powerful quake measuring 5.5 on the open-ended Richter scale struck the central and eastern coastal region of Venezuela on Wednesday afternoon toppling at least one large tower block.
The U.S. Geological Survey in Golden, Colorado, said it measured the quake at 6.9 on the Richter scale.
Caldera had planned to make an address on relations with Colombia at 8 p.m. (Midnight GMT) on Wednesday after two Venezuelan soldiers were seriously wounded in a cross-border attack.

Five soldiers on patrol were ambushed in the Paez district of Apure state, about two miles (three km) from the border, by presumed Colombian guerrillas. Two paratroopers were seriously wounded in the hour-long gunbattle that ensued, Defence Minister Tito Rincon Bravo said.
It was the most serious attack along the frontier since two soldiers were killed by Colombian rebels in April.

Caldera's speech was intended to focus on the recent attacks and to clarify his position on recent overtures made by Colombian guerrilla groups wanting to start a dialogue with the Venezuelan government.
